app_documentation:
QuickStock Real-Time Inventory Manager is a mobile-first Progressive Web App (PWA) for small retail stores. It replaces manual stock counts and spreadsheets with fast barcode-driven inventory control that stays in sync across every device in the store. The main purpose is to help staff find and update products in seconds, avoid selling out-of-stock items, and reorder before items run out. It is built with React on the front end, a Node.js REST API with WebSockets for live updates, and a PostgreSQL database, and it works on web and mobile web.

The MVP delivers four features. F1 Barcode Scanning (High priority) lets users scan with a device camera (ZXing), a handheld scanner or manual entry. Product details appear within 1 second, and unknown barcodes prompt the user to create a new product. F2 Real-Time Stock Tracking (High priority) pushes stock changes from sales, receipts, adjustments and damaged-goods entries to all connected devices within 2 seconds at 50 concurrent users. F3 Low-Stock Alerts and Reordering (Medium priority) lets managers set per-item reorder thresholds, generates alerts within 1 minute of a breach, suggests reorder quantities, supports snoozing and lets a reorder list be shared with a supplier. F4 Inventory Reports and Audit History (Medium priority) provides stock, sales and turnover reports for a chosen date range, generated within 5 seconds and exportable as CSV. It also keeps an append-only history of every inventory change, recording user, time, item, quantity change and reason.

The intended users are Store Owners, who view reports, inventory value and low-stock notifications. Store Managers set thresholds, review audit history and manage reorders. Store Clerks scan items and update stock in about 3 taps after roughly 15 minutes of training. Optional Supplier accounts are read-only. Access is enforced through role-based permissions backed by roles, permissions and user-role tables, with salted password hashes and HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ for all traffic.

The UI has five bottom-navigation sections (Home, Scan, Stock, Alerts, Reports) and seven screens: Dashboard, Scan Barcode, Product Detail & Stock Update, Stock List, Low-Stock Alerts, and Reports & Audit History. It uses the Inter typeface and a blue, teal and slate palette with color-coded stock states. It meets WCAG AA contrast, uses 48px touch targets and pairs color with text labels. Non-functional targets are 99.5% monthly uptime and daily automated backups retained for 30 days. The database has 20 tables, covering products, barcodes, stock levels, sales, purchase orders, an append-only stock_movements audit log, low-stock alerts, notifications and report exports. Delivery follows the 14-task QuickStock MVP Plan (T1-T14) across DBA, Developer and Designer roles. The key risks to monitor are camera-scan reliability on iOS Safari PWAs, concurrent update races, WebSocket stability on poor store Wi-Fi, scope versus timeline, and limited PWA push-notification support.

glossary.PWA (Progressive Web App): A web application that can be installed and used on mobile devices like a native app, with a web manifest and service worker. QuickStock uses it to serve clerks, managers and owners on phones, tablets and desktops.
glossary.SKU (Stock Keeping Unit): A unique internal identifier assigned to each product, stored in products.sku and used alongside barcodes to find and track items.
glossary.Reorder Threshold: A configurable quantity per product. When quantity on hand falls below it, the system generates a low-stock alert with a suggested reorder quantity.
glossary.Audit History (Stock Movement): An append-only record of every inventory change, capturing the user, time, product, quantity change, before and after quantities and reason. It is stored in the stock_movements table for accountability.
glossary.Live Sync (WebSocket): Real-time two-way communication that pushes stock changes to all connected devices within 2 seconds. The Live Sync Indicator shows connection status, with 'Live' when connected and 'Reconnecting' when offline.
glossary.RBAC (Role-Based Access Control): A security model in which permissions are granted to roles (Store Owner, Store Manager, Store Clerk, Supplier read-only) and users receive access through their assigned roles.
